name: Shell Automation
certifications: LPIC-1 (Linux Professional Institute, shell scripting objectives)

beginner.summary: For system administrators, developers, testers and support engineers who use a terminal but have not written reliable scripts. Covers Bash 5 on Linux, WSL2 or macOS: running and permissioning scripts, variables and quoting, exit statuses, tests and branching, loops, arguments with getopts, input and here documents, redirection, functions, arrays, string handling, grep, sed and awk, safe file handling, debugging with ShellCheck and shfmt, and a log rotation and reporting utility as the capstone.
prerequisites: Can open a terminal and move around a file system with cd, ls and cat
Has a Linux, WSL2, macOS or container environment where Bash 4 or later can be installed
Can edit a text file in Visual Studio Code, nano or vim
outcomes: Write, permission and run Bash scripts that quote correctly and return meaningful exit statuses
Control flow with tests, case, loops, functions and arrays, and take input from arguments, prompts and files
Process text and files safely with grep, sed, awk, find and xargs
Lint, format and debug scripts with ShellCheck, shfmt and bash -x, and deliver a tested command-line utility

intermediate.summary: For engineers who write basic Bash and now need scripts that are safe to run unattended. Covers strict mode and its gaps, script structure and libraries, long-option parsing, traps and cleanup, logging, subshell semantics, advanced awk and sed, jq and yq, curl for APIs, parallel jobs, locking and idempotency, cron and systemd timers, SSH automation, snapshot backups, bats testing, POSIX portability, secrets and injection, CI with GitHub Actions, and a multi-host toolkit capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the beginner level or writes Bash scripts with functions, loops and getopts
Can use grep, sed, awk, find and ssh on the command line
Has Docker or two Linux hosts available for multi-host exercises and a GitHub account for CI exercises
outcomes: Build modular scripts with strict-mode discipline, traps, logging and tested argument parsing

days.lab_task: Deliver opsctl, a Bash platform with subcommands to back up a database, rotate logs and deploy a release atomically across 5 hosts with rollback, exporting metrics through the node_exporter textfile directory. Gates: ShellCheck clean, 40 bats tests, hadolint-clean image, SHA256SUMS with a signature, retry with backoff, flock protection and a runbook. Inject a failure on host 3 and show the rollout stop and roll back.
days.deliverable: Repository with source, tests, CI workflow, signed release artifacts, runbook and a recorded failure-injection demo
checks: Inject a failure on host 3 during a 5-host deploy
The rollout stops at host 3, hosts 1 and 2 are rolled back, hosts 4 and 5 are untouched and the exit status is 1
Open a pull request against the repository
ShellCheck, shfmt and 40 bats tests pass and the release artifacts include SHA256SUMS and a signature
Query the metrics endpoint after a normal run
Each job reports a last-success timestamp inside its scheduled interval
